   481→## Feature 6: AWS Nitro TEE Fallback
   482→
   483→### Current State
   484→
   485→CipherBox uses Phala Cloud as the primary TEE for IPNS republishing. AWS Nitro is specified as the fallback.
   486→
   487→### AWS Nitro Enclave Architecture
   488→
   489→AWS Nitro Enclaves run inside a special VM partition on EC2 instances. The enclave has no network access, no persistent storage -- it communicates only via a vsock channel with the parent EC2 instance.
   490→
   491→IMPORTANT: There is NO official JavaScript/TypeScript SDK for AWS Nitro Enclaves NSM (Nitro Security Module) API. The official SDK is Rust-only (`aws-nitro-enclaves-nsm-api` crate).
   492→
   493→### Recommended Architecture
   494→
   495→| Component                      | Technology                             | Language   |
   496→| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- | ---------- |
   497→| Enclave application            | Rust binary                            | Rust       |
   498→| Attestation                    | `aws-nitro-enclaves-nsm-api` crate     | Rust       |
   499→| ECIES decryption               | `ecies` Rust crate (secp256k1)         | Rust       |
   500→| Ed25519 IPNS signing           | `ed25519-dalek` crate                  | Rust       |
   501→| IPNS record creation           | Custom (port from `@cipherbox/crypto`) | Rust       |
   502→| Parent-enclave communication   | vsock                                  | Rust       |
   503→| Orchestrator (parent instance) | Node.js (NestJS)                       | TypeScript |
   504→| KMS integration                | `@aws-sdk/client-kms`                  | TypeScript |
   505→
   506→### New Dependencies
   507→
   508→For the NestJS orchestrator (parent EC2 instance):
   509→
   510→```bash
   511→cd apps/api && pnpm add @aws-sdk/client-kms @aws-sdk/client-ec2
   512→```
   513→
   514→| Package               | Version | Purpose                                 |
   515→| --------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------- |
   516→| `@aws-sdk/client-kms` | ^3.x    | KMS condition key attestation for Nitro |
   517→| `@aws-sdk/client-ec2` | ^3.x    | Enclave lifecycle management (optional) |
   518→
   519→For the enclave (Rust, separate from Node.js monorepo):
   520→
   521→```toml
   522→# Cargo.toml for enclave binary
   523→[dependencies]
   524→aws-nitro-enclaves-nsm-api = "0.4"
   525→ecies = { version = "0.2", default-features = false }
   526→ed25519-dalek = "2.1"
   527→serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
   528→serde_json = "1"
   529→nix = { version = "0.29", features = ["socket"] }  # vsock
   530→```
   531→
   532→### Integration with Existing System
   533→
   534→The NestJS backend already has:
   535→
   536→- `republish-schedule.entity.ts` -- Stores encryptedIpnsPrivateKey and keyEpoch
   537→- `tee-key-state.entity.ts` -- Tracks TEE key epochs
   538→- BullMQ for job scheduling
   539→
   540→The Nitro fallback can reuse the same republish scheduling infrastructure. The only change is routing republish jobs to Nitro instead of Phala when Phala is unavailable.
   541→
   542→### Phala Cloud SDK Update
   543→
   544→The existing Phala integration may benefit from updating to the latest dstack SDK:
   545→
   546→| Package             | Version | Purpose                                           |
   547→| ------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
   548→| `@phala/dstack-sdk` | latest  | TEE client SDK for attestation and key derivation |
   549→
   550→Note: Verify whether CipherBox currently uses `@phala/dstack-sdk` or a different Phala integration. The existing codebase should be checked.
   551→
   552→### What NOT to Do
   553→
   554→| Approach                          | Why Not                                                                                 |
   555→| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   556→| Run Node.js inside Nitro Enclave  | No official NSM API for JavaScript; would need WASM bridge. Rust is the supported path. |
   557→| Use community JS bindings for NSM | None exist that are production-quality                                                  |
   558→| Skip attestation                  | Defeats the purpose of TEE -- must verify enclave integrity                             |
   559→
   560→### Confidence: MEDIUM
   561→
   562→The Rust enclave binary is well-understood architecturally but represents a new build target for the project. The vsock communication protocol needs custom implementation. This is the highest-effort feature in M2.

   719→## Roadmap Implications
   720→
   721→### Phase Ordering (by dependency chain)
   722→
   723→1. **Versioning first** -- Lowest risk, no new dependencies, purely metadata schema work. Good warmup.
   724→2. **Search second** -- Small new dependencies (minisearch, idb), client-only, no API changes needed.
   725→3. **MFA third** -- Web3Auth config change is fast; CipherBox-level WebAuthn/TOTP needs new API endpoints.
   726→4. **Sharing fourth** -- Most complex feature, touches crypto, API, and UI. Needs the other features stable first.
   727→5. **Advanced sync fifth** -- Conflict resolution is best designed after sharing is working (sharing introduces multi-writer scenarios that inform conflict rules).
   728→6. **Nitro fallback sixth** -- Separate build target (Rust enclave), can be developed in parallel but should ship last.
   729→
   730→### Risk Assessment
   731→
   732→| Feature        | Risk                                           | Mitigation                                                          |
   733→| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   734→| Sharing        | MEDIUM -- Protocol design complexity           | Prototype key re-wrapping first, validate with test vectors         |
   735→| Search         | LOW -- Well-understood pattern                 | MiniSearch is battle-tested                                         |
   736→| MFA            | LOW-MEDIUM -- Web3Auth pricing dependency      | Verify SCALE plan pricing; fallback to CipherBox-level MFA          |
   737→| Versioning     | LOW -- Metadata extension only                 | Keep version chain short (max 50) to avoid metadata bloat           |
   738→| Advanced Sync  | MEDIUM-HIGH -- Conflict resolution edge cases  | Extensive test matrix; start with last-writer-wins, evolve          |
   739→| Nitro Fallback | HIGH -- New language (Rust enclave), new infra | Prototype vsock communication early; consider hiring Rust expertise |

    54→## Recommended Testing Setup (for future implementation)
    55→
    56→### Philosophy
    57→
    58→CipherBox shall employ a **Test Pyramid** approach with comprehensive coverage at all layers. Backend and TEE development **must** follow **Test-Driven Development (TDD)**, while frontend relies on **End-to-End automation** for validation.
    59→
    60→**Core Principles:**
    61→- TDD is mandatory for all backend and TEE code - write tests first, then implementation
    62→- Test Pyramid structure: more unit tests, fewer E2E tests for fast feedback loops
    63→- All tests must run in CI/CD pipeline - no manual testing gates
    64→- Cryptographic operations require exhaustive testing with 100% coverage
    65→- Frontend coverage achieved through automated E2E browser tests (no TDD required)
    66→
    67→### Test Pyramid Structure
    68→
    69→**Target Ratios:**
    70→- Unit Tests: 70% of test suite
    71→- Integration Tests: 20% of test suite
    72→- E2E Tests: 10% of test suite
    73→
    74→**Layer Definitions:**
    75→
    76→| Layer | Scope | Speed | Dependencies |
    77→|-------|-------|-------|--------------|
    78→| Unit | Single function/class | < 5ms | All mocked |
    79→| Integration | Service composition, DB | 50-500ms | Real database, mocked externals |
    80→| API E2E | Full backend stack | 100ms-2s | Full app, mocked IPFS |
    81→| Frontend E2E | Complete application | 2-30s | Full stack |
    82→
    83→### Test Execution Environments
    84→
    85→**Unit Tests:**
    86→- Run on: Developer machines, CI runners
    87→- Dependencies: All mocked (database, IPFS, external APIs)
    88→- Database: None (mocked)
    89→- Secrets: None required
    90→- Parallelization: Full parallel execution
    91→
    92→**Integration Tests:**
    93→- Run on: Developer machines (Docker), CI runners
    94→- Dependencies: Real PostgreSQL in Docker, mocked IPFS/Pinata
    95→- Database: Test database with migrations, truncated between test suites
    96→- Secrets: Test credentials only (never production)
    97→- Parallelization: Sequential due to shared database state
    98→
    99→**API E2E Tests:**
   100→- Run on: Developer machines, CI runners, optionally staging
   101→- Dependencies: Full NestJS application, real database, mocked IPFS
   102→- Database: Test database, reset between test suites
   103→- Secrets: Test JWT keys, mock Web3Auth tokens
   104→
   105→**Frontend E2E Tests (Cypress/Puppeteer):**
   106→- Run on: Developer machines, CI runners, **staging environment**
   107→- Dependencies: Frontend app + Backend API + Database (full stack)
   108→- Database: Seeded with test fixtures, reset to snapshot between spec files
   109→- Browsers: Chrome (primary), Firefox, Edge
   110→- Parallelization: Parallel specs via Cypress Cloud
   111→
   112→**TEE Tests:**
   113→- Local/CI: Mock enclave, attestation skipped, test keys
   114→- Staging: Real Phala testnet enclave, attestation verified, test keys (not production)
   115→
   116→### Framework Requirements
   117→
   118→*Note: This section specifies framework choices and requirements. Concrete configuration files and implementation examples will be created when the testing infrastructure is implemented.*
   119→
   120→**Backend (NestJS):**
   121→- Test Runner: Jest (NestJS default)
   122→- Mocking: `@nestjs/testing` module with Jest mocks
   123→- HTTP Testing: Supertest for API endpoint testing
   124→- Coverage: Jest/Istanbul with enforced thresholds
   125→
   126→**Frontend (React):**
   127→- E2E Framework: Cypress (recommended) or Puppeteer
   128→- Component Testing: Cypress Component Testing for complex components (optional)
   129→- Visual Regression: Percy integration (optional)
   130→
   131→**TEE (Rust):**

   133→- Integration: Custom mock enclave harness for local testing
   134→
   135→### TDD Requirements (Backend & TEE)
   136→
   137→**Mandatory Workflow - Red-Green-Refactor:**
   138→1. RED: Write a failing test for new functionality
   139→2. GREEN: Write minimal code to make the test pass
   140→3. REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests green
   141→4. COMMIT: After each green phase
   142→5. REPEAT: Next requirement
   143→
   144→**TDD Rules:**
   145→- No production code without a failing test first
   146→- Tests must fail for the right reason before implementing
   147→- Write the simplest code to pass the test
   148→- Refactor only when tests are green
   149→
   150→**What Backend Unit Tests Must Cover:**
   151→- Service methods in isolation
   152→- Controller request handling and response formatting
   153→- DTOs and validation logic
   154→- Utility functions (crypto, data conversion)
   155→- Guards and middleware
   156→- Error handling and edge cases
   157→
   158→### Frontend E2E Requirements
   159→
   160→**No TDD required** - coverage achieved through comprehensive browser automation.
   161→
   162→**Test Coverage Must Include:**
   163→- All critical user journeys (authentication, file upload/download, folder operations)
   164→- Error scenarios and recovery flows
   165→- Cross-browser compatibility (Chrome, Firefox, Edge)
   166→
   167→**Selector Strategy:**
   168→- Use `data-testid` attributes exclusively for test selectors
   169→- Avoid flaky selectors (timing-based, nth-child, CSS classes)
   170→
   171→**Test Organization:**
   172→- Group by feature area: `auth/`, `vault/`, `settings/`
   173→- Separate spec files per user journey
   174→- Shared fixtures for mock data and responses
   175→- Custom commands for common operations (login, createVault, uploadFile)

   199→**Frontend E2E Metrics:**

   207→
   208→### Mocking Guidelines
   209→
   210→**What to Mock:**
   211→- Database connections and queries (unit tests only)
   212→- IPFS client operations (network calls)
   213→- Pinata API calls
   214→- Web3Auth verification

   216→
   217→**What NOT to Mock:**
   218→- Cryptographic functions - always test real encryption/decryption
   219→- Data conversion utilities (hexToBytes, bytesToHex)

   221→
   222→### Automated Linting & Pre-commit Hooks
   223→
   224→**Pre-commit Hook Requirements:**
   225→- ESLint with `--max-warnings 0` (zero tolerance for lint errors)
   226→- Prettier formatting check
   227→- TypeScript type checking
   228→- Unit tests for changed files only (`jest --findRelatedTests`)
   229→- Cargo fmt and Clippy for Rust code
   230→
   231→**Pre-push Hook Requirements:**

   233→- Integration tests

   236→
   237→**Enforcement:**
   238→- Commits blocked if any check fails
   239→- No `eslint-disable` comments without PR justification
   240→- No `.skip()` or `.only()` in tests (enforced via ESLint rules)
   241→- Bypassing hooks (`--no-verify`) requires explicit justification in PR
   242→
   243→**CI Duplication:**
   244→- All pre-commit checks duplicated in CI pipeline
   245→- Catches bypassed hooks - bypassing locally only delays failure
   246→
   247→### CI Pipeline Structure
   248→
   249→**Stage 1: Lint & Type Check (parallel)**

   137→## IPFS/IPNS Integration Details
   138→
   139→**IPFS Operations (from PoC):**
   140→```typescript
   141→// Adding content
   142→const { cid } = await ctx.ipfs.add(content, { pin: false });
   143→
   144→// Fetching content
   145→const data = await collectChunks(ctx.ipfs.cat(cid));
   146→
   147→// Pinning
   148→await ctx.ipfs.pin.add(cid);
   149→await ctx.ipfs.pin.rm(cid);
   150→
   151→// Key management
   152→await ctx.ipfs.key.gen(keyName, { type: "ed25519" });
   153→await ctx.ipfs.key.rm(keyName);
   154→```
   155→
   156→**IPNS Operations (from PoC):**
   157→```typescript
   158→// Publishing
   159→await ctx.ipfs.name.publish(`/ipfs/${cid}`, {
   160→    key: ipnsKeyName,
   161→    allowOffline: true,
   162→});
   163→
   164→// Resolving
   165→for await (const result of ctx.ipfs.name.resolve(ipnsName, { nocache: true })) {
   166→    // Extract CID from result
   167→}
   168→```

   170→**Production Relay Model (Planned):**
   171→- Client signs IPNS records locally

1→# Architecture
     2→
     3→**Analysis Date:** 2026-01-20
     4→
     5→## Pattern Overview
     6→
     7→**Overall:** Specification-First / Pre-Implementation Technology Demonstrator
     8→
     9→**Key Characteristics:**
    10→- Complete specification documents define the target architecture before implementation
    11→- Single proof-of-concept (PoC) console harness validates core IPFS/IPNS and encryption flows
    12→- Layered E2E encryption with zero-knowledge server design
    13→- Client-side cryptographic operations with server acting as relay and storage proxy
    14→- Per-folder IPNS records enabling future modular sharing capabilities
    15→
    16→## Layers
    17→
    18→**Specification Layer:**
    19→- Purpose: Define complete system design, security model, and implementation contract
    20→- Location: `00-Preliminary-R&D/Documentation/`
    21→- Contains: PRD, technical architecture, API spec, data flows, client spec, implementation roadmap
    22→- Depends on: None (foundation documents)
    23→- Used by: All implementation code (when built)
    24→
    25→**Proof-of-Concept Layer:**
    26→- Purpose: Validate IPFS/IPNS assumptions and encryption flows end-to-end
    27→- Location: `00-Preliminary-R&D/poc/`
    28→- Contains: Single-file console harness demonstrating file/folder operations
    29→- Depends on: IPFS daemon, cryptographic libraries
    30→- Used by: Architecture validation only (not production)
    31→
    32→**Client Layer (Specified, Not Implemented):**
    33→- Purpose: Handle all encryption/decryption, key management, UI
    34→- Location: (Not yet created - see `00-Preliminary-R&D/Documentation/CLIENT_SPECIFICATION.md`)
    35→- Contains: React 18 web app, Tauri/Electron desktop app with FUSE
    36→- Depends on: Web3Auth SDK, Web Crypto API, CipherBox Backend API
    37→- Used by: End users
    38→
    39→**Backend Layer (Specified, Not Implemented):**
    40→- Purpose: Token management, IPFS/IPNS relay, vault metadata storage, TEE coordination
    41→- Location: (Not yet created - see `00-Preliminary-R&D/Documentation/API_SPECIFICATION.md`)
    42→- Contains: NestJS API with 15 endpoints
    43→- Depends on: PostgreSQL, Pinata API, Web3Auth JWKS, TEE providers
    44→- Used by: Client applications
    45→
    46→**TEE Layer (Specified, Not Implemented):**
    47→- Purpose: Automatic IPNS republishing without user devices online
    48→- Location: External services (Phala Cloud primary, AWS Nitro fallback)
    49→- Contains: Secure enclaves for IPNS key decryption and signing
    50→- Depends on: Backend republish schedule
    51→- Used by: Backend cron jobs
    52→
    53→## Data Flow
    54→
    55→**File Upload Flow:**
    56→
    57→1. Client generates random `fileKey` (256-bit AES)
    58→2. Client encrypts file content with AES-256-GCM
    59→3. Client wraps `fileKey` with user's `publicKey` via ECIES
    60→4. Client sends encrypted blob to backend (POST `/ipfs/add`)
    61→5. Backend relays to Pinata, returns CID
    62→6. Client updates folder metadata with new file entry
    63→7. Client encrypts metadata with `folderKey`
    64→8. Client signs IPNS record with folder's `ipnsPrivateKey`
    65→9. Client encrypts `ipnsPrivateKey` with TEE `publicKey` for republishing
    66→10. Client sends signed record + encrypted IPNS key to backend (POST `/ipns/publish`)
    67→11. Backend publishes to IPFS network and stores republish schedule
    68→
    69→**Authentication Flow:**
    70→
    71→1. User authenticates via Web3Auth (4 methods supported)
    72→2. Web3Auth derives deterministic ECDSA keypair (secp256k1)
    73→3. Client authenticates with CipherBox backend (JWT or SIWE signature)
    74→4. Backend verifies identity, issues access token (15min) + refresh token (7d)
    75→5. Backend returns encrypted vault keys and TEE public keys
    76→6. Client decrypts `rootFolderKey` using `privateKey`
    77→7. Session active until logout or token expiry
    78→
    79→**State Management:**
    80→- `privateKey`: Client RAM only, never persisted or transmitted
    81→- `rootFolderKey`: Server stores encrypted with ECIES, client decrypts on login
    82→- Folder/file keys: Stored encrypted in IPNS metadata records
    83→- `ipnsPrivateKey`: Client encrypts with TEE public key for republishing
    84→
    85→## Key Abstractions
    86→
    87→**Vault:**
    88→- Purpose: User's encrypted file storage namespace
    89→- Examples: Root folder IPNS record, associated metadata
    90→- Pattern: One vault per user, identified by `rootIpnsName`
    91→
    92→**Folder:**
    93→- Purpose: Encrypted container with child entries (files/folders)
    94→- Examples: Root folder, Documents, Archive (from PoC)
    95→- Pattern: Each folder has own IPNS keypair, `folderKey` for metadata encryption
    96→
    97→**File Entry:**
    98→- Purpose: Encrypted file reference within folder metadata
    99→- Examples: `hello.txt` in PoC
   100→- Pattern: Contains encrypted name, CID, wrapped `fileKey`, IV, encryption mode
   101→
   102→**TEE Key Epoch:**
   103→- Purpose: Rotation-safe TEE public key management
   104→- Examples: `currentEpoch`, `previousEpoch` for 4-week grace period
   105→- Pattern: Client encrypts IPNS keys with current epoch, TEE supports previous for migration
   106→
   107→## Entry Points
   108→
   109→**PoC Console Harness:**
   110→- Location: `00-Preliminary-R&D/poc/src/index.ts`
   111→- Triggers: `npm run start` or `tsx src/index.ts`
   112→- Responsibilities: Creates folder hierarchy, uploads/modifies/moves/deletes files, verifies IPNS resolution, cleans up (unpin, remove keys)
   113→
   114→**Planned Web Application:**
   115→- Location: (To be created)
   116→- Triggers: Browser navigation to `/auth`, `/vault`, `/settings`
   117→- Responsibilities: Authentication, file browser UI, encryption/decryption
   118→
   119→**Planned Backend API:**
   120→- Location: (To be created)
   121→- Triggers: HTTP requests to 15 endpoints
   122→- Responsibilities: Token management, IPFS/IPNS relay, vault storage, TEE coordination
   123→
   124→**Planned Desktop Application:**
   125→- Location: (To be created)
   126→- Triggers: App launch, FUSE mount at `~/CipherVault`
   127→- Responsibilities: Transparent file access, background sync
   128→
   129→## Error Handling
   130→
   131→**Strategy:** Fail-fast with explicit error messages
   132→
   133→**Patterns:**
   134→- PoC: Throws errors on failures, logs warnings for non-critical issues (e.g., pin removal)
   135→- Specified Backend: HTTP status codes with structured error responses
   136→- Specified Client: User-facing error messages, retry logic for transient failures
   137→- TEE Republish: Exponential backoff (30s -> 60s -> 120s -> 240s -> 300s max)
   138→
   139→## Cross-Cutting Concerns
   140→
   141→**Logging:**
   142→- PoC: Console logging with step markers (`=== Step Name ===`)
   143→- Backend (specified): Structured logging, no private keys in logs (Security criterion S8)
   144→
   145→**Validation:**
   146→- PoC: Runtime type checking via TypeScript
   147→- Backend (specified): Request validation via NestJS decorators
   148→- Client (specified): Input sanitization before encryption
   149→
   150→**Authentication:**
   151→- Two-phase: Web3Auth for key derivation, CipherBox backend for API tokens
   152→- Token rotation: Refresh tokens rotated on each use
   153→- Zero-knowledge: Backend never sees private keys or plaintext
   154→
   155→**Security Invariants:**
   156→- Private key exists only in client RAM, cleared on logout
   157→- All files encrypted with unique random key + IV (no deduplication)
   158→- Server stores only encrypted keys (ECIES wrapped)
   159→- TEE keys exist in enclave memory only for milliseconds during signing
   160→
   161→---
   162→

1→# Environment Architecture
     2→
     3→**Created:** 2026-01-25
     4→
     5→## Overview
     6→
     7→CipherBox requires isolated environments to prevent cross-environment interference, particularly with IPNS sequence numbers. This document defines the environment architecture and solves the Web3Auth key isolation problem.
     8→
     9→## The Problem
    10→
    11→**Current State:** All environments share the same Web3Auth project (SAPPHIRE_DEVNET) and client ID. This means:
    12→
    13→- Same user identity → same derived secp256k1 keypair → same Ed25519 IPNS keypair
    14→- IPNS records use monotonically increasing sequence numbers
    15→- If CI publishes seq=100, local dev (fresh DB) tries seq=1 → rejected by network/delegated routing
    16→- Test repeatability is impossible without manual intervention
    17→
    18→## Environment Matrix
    19→
    20→| Environment    | IPFS Mode      | Web3Auth Network | IPNS Routing           | Database            | TEE Republishing     | Isolation Level            |
    21→| -------------- | -------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------- |
    22→| **Local Dev**  | Kubo (offline) | Sapphire Devnet  | Mock service           | Local Postgres      | **Disabled**         | Full                       |
    23→| **CI E2E**     | Kubo (offline) | Sapphire Devnet  | Mock service (per-run) | Ephemeral Postgres  | **Disabled**         | Full per-run               |
    24→| **Staging**    | Kubo (online)  | Sapphire Devnet  | delegated-ipfs.dev     | Managed Postgres    | **Active** (testnet) | Shared with Local/CI users |
    25→| **Production** | Pinata         | Sapphire Mainnet | delegated-ipfs.dev     | Production Postgres | **Active** (mainnet) | Full                       |
    26→
    27→## Solution: Environment-Aware Key Derivation
    28→
    29→### Recommended Approach: Environment-Specific IPNS Key Derivation
    30→
    31→The IPNS keypair is derived from the user's vault key. By adding an environment-specific context (via the HKDF `info` parameter) to this derivation, we get different IPNS keys per environment while keeping the same Web3Auth identity.
    32→
    33→**Key Insight:** The problematic shared state is the **IPNS keypair**, not the user's encryption keypair. We can:
    34→
    35→1. Keep the same secp256k1 keypair from Web3Auth (same encryption keys)
    36→2. Add environment context only to Ed25519 IPNS key derivation (different IPNS identities)
    37→
    38→This means:
    39→
    40→- Same user can encrypt/decrypt files across environments (if CIDs are known)
    41→  - **Security Note:** CID leakage can expose test or production data across environments. Use separate test accounts/credentials for CI vs production, and sanitize or isolate test data to avoid accidental cross-environment access.
    42→- Different IPNS namespaces per environment → no sequence conflicts
    43→- Test accounts work in all environments without conflicts
    44→
    45→### Implementation
    46→
    47→```typescript
    48→// packages/crypto/src/ipns.ts
    49→
    50→// Fixed HKDF salt for domain separation (extract phase)
    51→const HKDF_SALT = 'CipherBox-IPNS-v1';
    52→
    53→// Environment context prefixes for HKDF info (expand phase)
    54→const ENVIRONMENT_CONTEXT = {
    55→  local: 'env:local',
    56→  ci: 'env:ci',
    57→  staging: 'env:staging',
    58→  production: 'env:production',
    59→} as const;
    60→
    61→type Environment = keyof typeof ENVIRONMENT_CONTEXT;
    62→
    63→export function deriveIpnsKeypair(
    64→  userSecp256k1PrivateKey: Uint8Array,
    65→  folderId: string,
    66→  environment: Environment
    67→): { publicKey: Uint8Array; privateKey: Uint8Array } {
    68→  // HKDF-SHA256: Fixed salt for domain separation, environment/folder in info for context binding
    69→  // This follows RFC 5869 best practices and matches existing deriveKey patterns in the codebase
    70→  const info = `${ENVIRONMENT_CONTEXT[environment]}:folder:${folderId}`;
    71→  // ... derivation logic using HKDF(IKM=userSecp256k1PrivateKey, salt=HKDF_SALT, info=info)
    72→}
    73→```
    74→
    75→**Configuration:**
    76→
    77→```bash
    78→# .env
    79→CIPHERBOX_ENVIRONMENT=local  # local | ci | staging | production
    80→```
    81→
    82→### Alternative: Separate Web3Auth Projects
    83→
    84→If you prefer complete user isolation (different user databases per environment):
    85→
    86→| Environment | Web3Auth Project  | Network          | Client ID  |
    87→| ----------- | ----------------- | ---------------- | ---------- |
    88→| Local/CI    | cipherbox-dev     | Sapphire Devnet  | `BK...dev` |
    89→| Staging     | cipherbox-staging | Sapphire Devnet  | `BK...stg` |
    90→| Production  | cipherbox-prod    | Sapphire Mainnet | `BK...prd` |
    91→
    92→**Pros:**
    93→
    94→- Complete isolation including encryption keys
    95→- No code changes needed (just config)
    96→- Clear separation of concerns
    97→
    98→**Cons:**
    99→
   100→- Need separate test accounts per environment
   101→- Can't share encrypted data between environments
   102→- More Web3Auth dashboard management
   103→
   104→## Detailed Environment Specifications
   105→
   106→### 1. Local Development Environment
   107→
   108→**Purpose:** Isolated development with persistent state, no network dependencies
   109→
   110→**Infrastructure:**
   111→
   112→```yaml
   113→# docker/docker-compose.local.yml
   114→services:
   115→  postgres:
   116→    image: postgres:16-alpine
   117→    environment:
   118→      POSTGRES_DB: cipherbox_local
   119→    ports:
   120→      - '5432:5432'
   121→    volumes:
   122→      - postgres_local_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
   123→
   124→  ipfs:
   125→    image: ipfs/kubo:v0.34.0
   126→    command: daemon --offline # KEY: Offline mode
   127→    ports:
   128→      - '127.0.0.1:5001:5001' # API
   129→      - '127.0.0.1:8080:8080' # Gateway
   130→    volumes:
   131→      - ipfs_local_data:/data/ipfs
   132→
   133→  mock-ipns-routing:

   136→      - '127.0.0.1:3001:3001'

   422→## TEE Infrastructure by Environment
   423→
   424→The TEE (Trusted Execution Environment) layer handles IPNS republishing to prevent record expiry (24-hour TTL). This section defines TEE requirements per environment.
   425→
   426→### TEE Environment Matrix
   427→
   428→| Environment    | TEE Infrastructure     | IPNS Republishing | Monitoring        | Cleanup                    |
   429→| -------------- | ---------------------- | ----------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------- |
   430→| **Local Dev**  | None                   | Not needed        | None              | User resets to clean slate |
   431→| **CI E2E**     | None                   | Not needed        | None              | Ephemeral per-run          |
   432→| **Staging**    | Active (Phala testnet) | Every 3 hours     | Integration tests | Periodic DHT cleanup       |
   433→| **Production** | Active (Phala mainnet) | Every 3 hours     | Full alerting     | Automated stale detection  |
   434→
   435→### Local Development: No TEE
   436→
   437→**Rationale:**
   438→
   439→- IPNS records stored in mock routing service (persistent volume)
   440→- No real DHT propagation = no expiry concerns
   441→- Users working on non-TEE features don't need republishing complexity
   442→- If IPNS state becomes corrupted, user can reset: `docker-compose down -v && docker-compose up`
   443→
   444→**Configuration:**
   445→
   446→```bash
   447→# apps/api/.env.local
   448→TEE_ENABLED=false
   449→# No TEE_* environment variables needed
   450→```
   451→
   452→**When working on TEE features locally:**
   453→
   454→- Use staging environment for TEE development/testing
   455→- Or run mock TEE service (future: `tools/mock-tee-service`)
   456→

   458→
   459→**Rationale:**
   460→
   461→- Test runs complete in minutes, well within 24-hour IPNS TTL
   462→- No benefit to republishing during test execution
   463→- Mock IPNS routing service resets per-run (no accumulated state)
   464→- Simpler CI pipeline without TEE service dependencies

   466→**Configuration:**

   470→env:

   472→  # No TEE service container needed

   475→**E2E Test Considerations:**

   477→- Tests should NOT depend on IPNS records surviving between test runs

   640→## IPNS Staleness Incident Runbook
   641→
   642→### Symptoms
   643→
   644→- Users report "folder not found" or stale data
   645→- Monitoring shows records >20h since republish
   646→
   647→### Diagnosis
   648→

   650→2. Check backend cron status: `systemctl status cipherbox-republish`
   651→3. Query stale records: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM folder_ipns WHERE last_republish_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '20 hours'`
   652→

   654→

   656→2. If cron stopped: Restart cron, monitor catch-up
   657→3. If specific records failing: Check encryptedIpnsPrivateKey validity, may need user to re-publish
   658→
   659→### User Communication
   660→
   661→- <20h stale: No user impact, monitor
   662→- 20-24h stale: Prepare user comms, accelerate fix
   663→- > 24h stale: IPNS records expired, users must re-publish from client
   664→```

   666→### TEE Key Encryption Architecture
   667→
   668→This section documents the security architecture for encrypting IPNS private keys before transmission to the TEE for republishing.
   669→
   670→#### Threat Model
   671→
   672→**Assets:**
   673→
   674→- IPNS private keys (Ed25519) - control over user's folder metadata
   675→- User's ability to update IPNS records
   676→
   677→**Threats:**
   678→
   679→1. **Network interception:** Attacker intercepts IPNS private key in transit to TEE
   680→2. **TEE key compromise:** Attacker obtains TEE private key, can decrypt all `encryptedIpnsPrivateKey` values
   681→3. **Stale epoch attack:** Attacker replays old encrypted keys after epoch rotation
   682→
   683→**Security Goals:**
   684→
   685→- IPNS private keys are never transmitted in plaintext
   686→- Only the current TEE can decrypt keys (forward secrecy via epoch rotation)
   687→- Key compromise has bounded impact (4-week epoch window)
   688→
   689→#### Encryption Flow
   690→
   691→```text
   692→User Client                      CipherBox API                    TEE (Phala Cloud)
   693→    |                                 |                                 |
   694→    |  1. Fetch TEE public key        |                                 |
   695→    |-------------------------------->|                                 |
   696→    |                                 |  2. Get current epoch key       |
   697→    |                                 |-------------------------------->|
   698→    |                                 |<--------------------------------|
   699→    |<--------------------------------|  {publicKey, epoch}             |
   700→    |                                 |                                 |
   701→    |  3. ECIES encrypt IPNS key      |                                 |
   702→    |  with TEE public key            |                                 |
   703→    |                                 |                                 |
   704→    |  4. POST /folders/:id/publish   |                                 |
   705→    |  {encryptedIpnsPrivateKey,      |                                 |
   706→    |   keyEpoch, ipnsValue, ...}     |                                 |
   707→    |-------------------------------->|                                 |
   708→    |                                 |  5. Store for republishing      |
   709→    |                                 |  (cron every 3 hours)           |
   710→    |                                 |                                 |
   711→    |                                 |  6. Send encrypted key to TEE   |
   712→    |                                 |-------------------------------->|
   713→    |                                 |                                 |  7. Decrypt in hardware
   714→    |                                 |                                 |  8. Sign IPNS record
   715→    |                                 |                                 |  9. Discard key (never stored)
   716→    |                                 |<--------------------------------|
   717→    |                                 |  {signedIpnsRecord}             |
   718→```
   719→
   720→#### Encryption Primitive: ECIES over secp256k1
   721→
   722→Per project security standards, IPNS private keys MUST be encrypted using ECIES (Elliptic Curve Integrated Encryption Scheme) with secp256k1:
   723→
   724→```typescript
   725→// packages/crypto/src/tee/encrypt.ts
   726→import { eciesEncrypt } from '../ecies';
   727→
   728→export async function encryptIpnsKeyForTee(
   729→  ipnsPrivateKey: Uint8Array, // 32-byte Ed25519 private key
   730→  teePublicKey: Uint8Array, // secp256k1 public key (33 or 65 bytes)
   731→  keyEpoch: number // Current TEE key epoch
   732→): Promise<EncryptedIpnsKey> {
   733→  // ECIES encryption: ephemeral ECDH + AES-256-GCM
   734→  const ciphertext = await eciesEncrypt(ipnsPrivateKey, teePublicKey);
   735→
   736→  return {
   737→    ciphertext,
   738→    keyEpoch,
   739→    algorithm: 'ECIES-secp256k1-AES256GCM',
   740→  };
   741→}
   742→```
   743→
   744→#### TEE Public Key Distribution
   745→
   746→The TEE public key is obtained via the CipherBox API, which caches and validates it from Phala Cloud:
   747→
   748→```typescript
   749→// apps/api/src/tee/tee.service.ts
   750→export class TeeService {
   751→  private cachedPublicKey: { key: Uint8Array; epoch: number; expiresAt: Date } | null = null;
   752→
   753→  async getCurrentPublicKey(): Promise<{ publicKey: Uint8Array; epoch: number }> {
   754→    // 1. Check cache (valid for 1 hour)
   755→    if (this.cachedPublicKey && this.cachedPublicKey.expiresAt > new Date()) {
   756→      return { publicKey: this.cachedPublicKey.key, epoch: this.cachedPublicKey.epoch };
   757→    }
   758→
   759→    // 2. Fetch from Phala Cloud with attestation verification
   760→    const response = await this.phalaClient.getPublicKey();
   761→
   762→    // 3. Verify attestation quote (proves key is from genuine TEE)
   763→    await this.verifyAttestation(response.attestation);
   764→
   765→    // 4. Cache with expiry
   766→    this.cachedPublicKey = {
   767→      key: response.publicKey,
   768→      epoch: response.epoch,
   769→      expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 60 * 60 * 1000), // 1 hour
   770→    };
   771→
   772→    return { publicKey: response.publicKey, epoch: response.epoch };
   773→  }
   774→}
   775→```
   776→
   777→#### Key Epoch Rotation Scheme
   778→
   779→TEE keys rotate every 4 weeks (`TEE_KEY_EPOCH_ROTATION_WEEKS=4`) with a 1-week grace period:
   780→
   781→| Epoch State      | Window    | API Behavior                                     |
   782→| ---------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
   783→| Current          | Weeks 0-4 | Normal processing                                |
   784→| Previous (grace) | Weeks 4-5 | Accept, re-encrypt with new epoch, update record |
   785→| Expired          | >5 weeks  | Reject with `EPOCH_EXPIRED` error                |
   786→
   787→**Epoch Handling Logic:**
   788→
   789→```typescript
   790→// apps/api/src/tee/epoch.service.ts
   791→export class EpochService {
   792→  private readonly GRACE_PERIOD_WEEKS = 1;
   793→
   794→  async validateEpoch(submittedEpoch: number): Promise<EpochValidation> {
   795→    const currentEpoch = await this.getCurrentEpoch();
   796→
   797→    if (submittedEpoch === currentEpoch) {
   798→      return { valid: true, action: 'PROCESS_NORMALLY' };
   799→    }
   800→
   801→    if (submittedEpoch === currentEpoch - 1) {
   802→      const gracePeriodEnd = this.getEpochEndDate(currentEpoch - 1).add(
   803→        this.GRACE_PERIOD_WEEKS,
   804→        'weeks'
   805→      );
   806→
   807→      if (new Date() < gracePeriodEnd) {
   808→        return { valid: true, action: 'RE_ENCRYPT_AND_UPDATE' };
   809→      }
   810→    }
   811→
   812→    return {
   813→      valid: false,
   814→      action: 'REJECT',
   815→      error: {
   816→        code: 'EPOCH_EXPIRED',
   817→        message: 'TEE key epoch expired. Fetch new TEE public key and re-encrypt.',
   818→        currentEpoch,
   819→      },
   820→    };
   821→  }
   822→}
   823→```
   824→
   825→**Grace Period Expiration:**
   826→Records encrypted with an expired epoch that were not re-encrypted during the grace period become invalid. The TEE cannot decrypt them, and the republishing job will:
   827→
   828→1. Mark the record as `republish_failed` with reason `EPOCH_EXPIRED`
   829→2. Send alert to monitoring (PagerDuty/Opsgenie)
   830→3. User must re-publish from client to restore republishing
   831→
   832→#### Forward Secrecy Considerations
   833→
   834→- **Epoch rotation provides bounded compromise:** If a TEE private key is compromised, only records encrypted with that epoch's key are exposed
   835→- **No retroactive decryption:** Old epoch keys are destroyed; past ciphertexts cannot be decrypted
   836→- **Grace period tradeoff:** 1-week grace period balances usability (client update propagation) vs security (exposure window)
   837→

   868→## Appendix: Alternative Approaches Considered
   869→
   870→### A. Fully Separate Web3Auth Projects per Environment
   871→
   872→**Approach:** Create 4 separate Web3Auth projects (local, ci, staging, prod)
   873→
   874→**Rejected because:**
   875→
   876→- Overhead of managing 4 projects
   877→- Need separate test accounts per environment
   878→- Can't share test fixtures between local/CI/staging
   879→- Environment context achieves same isolation with less complexity
   880→
   881→### B. Backend User Aggregation (Custom Auth)
   882→
   883→**Approach:** Backend issues environment-specific tokens, client presents to Web3Auth via Custom Auth
   884→
   885→**Rejected because:**
   886→
   887→- Significant implementation complexity
   888→- Custom Auth provider setup required
   889→- Adds latency to auth flow
   890→- Over-engineered for the actual problem
   891→
   892→### C. IPNS Sequence Reset via Admin API
   893→
   894→**Approach:** Reset IPNS sequence numbers between test runs
   895→
   896→**Rejected because:**
   897→
   898→- IPNS sequence is network-wide, can't be reset
   899→- Would require deleting/recreating IPNS keys
   900→- Loses data in the process
   901→- Doesn't solve the fundamental isolation problem

    32→## Terminology Standards

    34→Always use consistent terminology:

    49→## Critical Security Rules
    50→
    51→1. **Never** suggest storing `privateKey` in localStorage/sessionStorage
    52→2. **Never** suggest logging sensitive keys
    53→3. **Never** suggest sending unencrypted keys to server
    54→4. **Always** use ECIES for key wrapping
    55→5. **Always** use AES-256-GCM for content encryption
    56→6. The server NEVER has access to plaintext or unencrypted keys
    57→7. **Always** encrypt `ipnsPrivateKey` with TEE public key before sending for republishing
    58→8. TEE decrypts IPNS keys in hardware only, signs, and immediately discards

    60→## API Development Workflow
    61→
    62→When working on `apps/api` code:
    63→
    64→1. **After modifying API endpoints, DTOs, or controllers**, regenerate the API client to keep the web app in sync:
    65→
    66→   ```bash
    67→   pnpm api:generate
    68→   ```
    69→
    70→   This command generates the OpenAPI spec from the API, creates the typed client for the web app, and runs lint fixes.

    72→2. **Always run `pnpm api:generate` before completing a feature** that touches the API to ensure type safety across the monorepo.

    74→3. **Commit the regenerated client files** (`apps/web/src/api/`) along with your API changes.

    76→## Code Generation Guidelines
    77→
    78→When generating code for CipherBox:
    79→
    80→1. Use TypeScript for all JavaScript code
    81→2. Use `Uint8Array` for binary data, not strings
    82→3. Use Web Crypto API for browser encryption
    83→4. Use camelCase for API fields, snake_case for database columns
    84→5. Include proper error handling for crypto operations
    85→6. Clear sensitive data from memory after use

    87→## Architecture Decisions
    88→
    89→- **Auth:** Web3Auth for key derivation, CipherBox backend for tokens
    90→- **Storage:** IPFS via Pinata for files, IPNS for metadata (all relayed via CipherBox API)
    91→- **Encryption:** Client-side only, server is zero-knowledge
    92→- **Sync:** IPNS polling (30s interval), no push infrastructure
    93→- **Desktop:** FUSE mount for transparent file access
    94→- **TEE Republishing:** Phala Cloud (primary) / AWS Nitro (fallback) for automatic IPNS republishing every 3 hours
    95→- **Key Epochs:** TEE public keys rotate with 4-week grace period for seamless migration

   113→**ALWAYS attempt to verify application changes using Playwright MCP** when it is available. This ensures implemented features work correctly at runtime.

   115→**When to use Playwright MCP:**

   126→// 1. Navigate to the app

   175→## Git Workflow
   176→
   177→**Branch Protection Rules:**
   178→
   179→- **NEVER push directly to `main` branch** - all changes must go through feature branches and PRs
   180→- Create feature branches with descriptive names (e.g., `feat/add-auth`, `fix/ipns-publish`)
   181→- All commits should be made on feature branches first
   182→- Merge to main only via pull requests
   183→
   184→**Branch Naming:**
   185→
   186→- `feat/` - New features
   187→- `fix/` - Bug fixes
   188→- `docs/` - Documentation updates
   189→- `refactor/` - Code refactoring
   190→- `chore/` - Maintenance tasks
   191→
   192→**Commit Messages:**
   193→
   194→Commits must follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format. This is enforced by commitlint via a husky `commit-msg` hook.
   195→
   196→```text
   197→type(optional-scope): description
   198→
   199→[optional body]
   200→```
   201→
   202→Valid types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`. Any scope string is allowed (e.g., `feat(api): add health endpoint`).
   203→
   204→**Releases & Versioning:**
   205→
   206→- All packages share a single unified version (currently tracked in `.release-please-manifest.json`)
   207→- [Release Please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please) automates changelog generation, version bumping, and GitHub Releases
   208→- On push to `main`, the `release-please.yml` workflow creates/updates a release PR with accumulated changes
   209→- When that PR is merged, Release Please creates a GitHub Release and `vX.Y.Z` tag
   210→- Version bumps propagate to all `package.json` files, `Cargo.toml`, and `tauri.conf.json` via `release-please-config.json`
   211→- Staging deploys are triggered by pushing a tag matching `v*-staging*`. Legacy tags (e.g., `v0.1.0-staging.1`) also match but the **recommended convention** for new tags is `v<version>-staging-rc-<N>` (e.g., `v0.1.2-staging-rc-1`, `v0.1.2-staging-rc-2`). The `rc-N` suffix is a sequential counter allowing multiple staging deploys per version.

    96→## CipherBox Security Model
    97→
    98→This project implements zero-knowledge encrypted storage. Key security properties:
    99→
   100→**Trust Model:**
   101→- Client: Fully trusted (user's device)
   102→- Server: Untrusted (zero-knowledge, never sees plaintext or keys)
   103→- TEE: Trusted for IPNS republishing only (hardware isolation)
   104→- IPFS/Pinata: Untrusted (only sees ciphertext)
   105→
   106→**Key Hierarchy:**
   107→```
   108→User Private Key (secp256k1, from Web3Auth)
   109→    └── Root Folder Key (derived, AES-256)
   110→        └── Folder Keys (per-folder, AES-256)
   111→            └── File Keys (per-file, AES-256)
   112→```
   113→
   114→**Critical Rules:**
   115→- ECIES for key wrapping
   116→- AES-256-GCM for content encryption
   117→- Web Crypto API only (no JS crypto libraries)
   118→- Uint8Array for all binary data
   119→- Never expose keys to server
   120→- TEE receives only encrypted IPNS keys

---
created: 2026-02-14T00:00
title: Add bring-your-own IPFS node support
area: api
files:
  - apps/api/src/ipfs/ipfs.module.ts
  - apps/api/src/ipfs/providers/ipfs-provider.interface.ts
  - apps/api/src/ipfs/providers/local.provider.ts
  - apps/api/src/ipfs/providers/pinata.provider.ts
  - apps/api/.env.example
  - apps/web/src/lib/api/ipfs.ts
---

## Problem

Currently CipherBox supports two IPFS providers: Pinata (production default) and a local Kubo node (dev/testing). Both are configured server-side via environment variables (`IPFS_PROVIDER`, `IPFS_LOCAL_API_URL`). There is no way for end users to bring their own IPFS node — the choice is made by the server operator, not the individual user.

For a zero-knowledge privacy tool, users may want to:

- Pin their encrypted data to their own IPFS node (self-sovereignty)
- Use a preferred pinning service other than Pinata (e.g., web3.storage, Filebase, nft.storage)
- Run a personal Kubo/IPFS node at home and have CipherBox pin directly to it
- Avoid relying on a third-party pinning service entirely

This requires a user-level IPFS configuration (not just server-level env vars) and potentially a hybrid model where the backend can relay uploads to a user-specified IPFS endpoint, or the client uploads directly to the user's node.

## Solution

TBD — key design questions to resolve:

1. **Client-direct vs server-relay:** Should the web app upload encrypted blobs directly to the user's IPFS node (bypassing backend), or should the backend proxy to the user's configured endpoint?
   - Client-direct: simpler, no server load, but CORS/connectivity issues
   - Server-relay: consistent quota tracking, but server sees user's IPFS credentials

2. **User settings model:** Add per-user IPFS config (endpoint URL, auth token, provider type) stored in user settings. UI for configuring custom node in settings page.

3. **Provider abstraction:** The existing `IpfsProviderInterface` (pin/unpin/fetch) is already well-abstracted. A new "user-custom" provider that reads config from user settings rather than env vars would slot in cleanly.

4. **IPNS implications:** If user pins to their own node, IPNS republishing and delegated routing need to work with the user's node or be handled differently.

5. **Quota tracking:** If uploads go directly to user's node, server-side quota tracking becomes optional or advisory.

6. **Fallback/reliability:** What happens if user's node is unreachable? Fallback to default provider, or fail?

7. **Conflict detection:** Phase 16 (M2) adds API-level optimistic concurrency for conflict detection — the API checks IPNS sequence numbers on publish. BYO-IPFS bypasses the API for publishes, so this conflict detection mechanism will stop working. This feature will need a client-side conflict detection strategy (e.g., IPNS resolution before publish, or CRDT-based metadata) when BYO-IPFS is implemented.

  - Usage: `00-Preliminary-R&D/poc/src/index.ts`

**Pinata (Implemented in PoC, optional):**
- Remote IPFS pinning service - Persistent file storage
  - SDK/Client: Native `fetch` API
  - Auth: `PINATA_API_KEY`, `PINATA_API_SECRET` env vars
  - Toggle: `PINATA_ENABLED=true`
  - Endpoints used:
    - `POST https://api.pinata.cloud/pinning/pinByHash` - Pin CID
    - `DELETE https://api.pinata.cloud/pinning/unpin/{cid}` - Unpin CID
  - Usage: `pinataPin()`, `pinataUnpin()` in `00-Preliminary-R&D/poc/src/index.ts`

**Web3Auth (Planned - Not Implemented):**
- Authentication and key derivation - User identity
  - SDK/Client: `@web3auth/modal` (planned)
  - Auth methods: Google, Apple, GitHub, Email, Magic Link, External Wallet
  - JWKS endpoint: `https://api-auth.web3auth.io/jwks`
  - Key feature: Group connections for deterministic keypair derivation
  - Spec: `00-Preliminary-R&D/Documentation/TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md` Section 2

# CipherBox AI Agent Instructions

## Version Management

**Current Documentation Version:** 1.10.0
**Status:** Finalized (2026-01-20)

### ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Do Not Edit Preliminary/Documentation Files

All files in `Preliminary/Documentation/` are **FINALIZED** specifications (version 1.10.0, status: Finalized). These documents represent the agreed-upon design and should **NOT** be modified.

**If you need to make changes:**

- New implementation documentation should be created in a separate location
- Working notes and updates belong in `.planning/` or project-specific directories
- Do not modify version numbers or content in `Preliminary/Documentation/`

---

## Project Overview

**CipherBox** is a **technology demonstrator** for privacy-first, zero-knowledge encrypted cloud storage using IPFS/IPNS for decentralized persistence and Web3Auth for deterministic key derivation.

**Purpose:** This is not a commercial product. It demonstrates novel applications of cryptography and decentralized systems.

**Core Principle:** The server NEVER sees plaintext data or unencrypted keys. All encryption/decryption happens client-side.

## Documentation Structure

| Document                                                                            | Purpose                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| [PRD.md](../Preliminary/Documentation/PRD.md)                                       | Product requirements, user journeys, scope |
| [TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md](../Preliminary/Documentation/TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md) | Encryption, key hierarchy, system design   |
| [API_SPECIFICATION.md](../Preliminary/Documentation/API_SPECIFICATION.md)           | Backend endpoints, database schema         |
| [DATA_FLOWS.md](../Preliminary/Documentation/DATA_FLOWS.md)                         | Sequence diagrams, test vectors            |
| [CLIENT_SPECIFICATION.md](../Preliminary/Documentation/CLIENT_SPECIFICATION.md)     | Web UI, desktop app specs                  |
| [IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md](../Preliminary/Documentation/IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md) | Week-by-week development plan              |

---

## Critical Architecture Patterns

### Two-Phase Authentication Model

CipherBox uses a **mandatory two-phase auth flow** that must be understood before implementing any auth-related features:

1. **Phase 1 (Web3Auth):** User authenticates → Web3Auth derives ECDSA secp256k1 keypair via threshold cryptography
2. **Phase 2 (CipherBox Backend):** Client authenticates with backend using either:
   - **Option A:** Web3Auth ID token (JWT) validated via JWKS endpoint
   - **Option B:** SIWE-like signature flow (nonce-based)

**Key Insight:** The ECDSA keypair from Phase 1 is the user's identity. Web3Auth's "group connections" feature ensures that Google OAuth, email/password, magic links, and external wallet auth all derive the **same keypair** for the same user.

### Zero-Knowledge Key Hierarchy

```text
User Auth → Web3Auth → ECDSA Private Key (client RAM only, never transmitted)
                    ├─ Used for ECIES decryption of all data keys
                    ├─ Used to decrypt IPNS signing keys (Ed25519)
                    └─ Destroyed on logout

ECDSA Public Key (stored on server, identifies user)
    └─ Used to encrypt (ECIES):
        ├─ Root Folder Key (AES-256, stored encrypted on server)
        ├─ Subfolder Keys (AES-256, stored encrypted in parent IPNS metadata)
        └─ File Keys (AES-256, stored encrypted in folder IPNS metadata)
```

**Critical Rule:** Never log, persist to disk, or transmit the ECDSA private key. It exists ONLY in client memory during the session.

### Per-Folder IPNS Architecture

Each folder has its own IPNS entry containing encrypted metadata. This design enables future per-folder sharing (v2+).

**Folder Metadata Structure:**

```typescript
interface DecryptedFolderMetadata {
  children: Array<{
    type: 'file' | 'folder';
    nameEncrypted: string; // AES-256-GCM(name, folderKey)
    nameIv: string;
    cid?: string; // For files: IPFS CID
    ipnsName?: string; // For folders: IPNS name
    fileKeyEncrypted?: string; // ECIES(fileKey, userPubkey)
    subfolderKeyEncrypted?: string; // ECIES(folderKey, userPubkey)
    size?: number;
    created: number;
    modified: number;
  }>;
}
```

**When modifying files/folders:** Always re-encrypt and republish the containing folder's IPNS entry.

## Technology Stack & Standards

### Encryption Primitives (Non-Negotiable)

| Algorithm           | Use Case                            | Implementation                |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| **AES-256-GCM**     | File content + metadata encryption  | Web Crypto API / libsodium.js |
| **ECIES secp256k1** | Key wrapping (files, folders)       | ethers.js / libsodium.js      |
| **ECDSA secp256k1** | IPNS signing, user identity         | Web3Auth / ethers.js          |
| **HKDF-SHA256**     | Key derivation                      | Web Crypto API                |
| **Argon2**          | Password hashing (server-side only) | argon2-browser                |

**Never use:** Custom crypto, CBC mode, ECB mode, MD5, SHA1

### Target Tech Stack (v1.0)

- **Frontend:** React 18 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS
- **Backend:** Node.js + NestJS + TypeScript
- **Database:** PostgreSQL (users, vaults, audit trail)
- **Storage:** IPFS via Pinata API
- **Auth:** Web3Auth Modal SDK (@web3auth/modal)
- **Desktop:** Tauri/Electron + FUSE (macFUSE/FUSE3/WinFSP)

## Development Patterns

### API Development Workflow

When working on `apps/api` code:

1. **After modifying API endpoints, DTOs, or controllers**, regenerate the API client to keep the web app in sync:

   ```bash
   pnpm api:generate
   ```

   This command generates the OpenAPI spec from the API, creates the typed client for the web app, and runs lint fixes.

2. **Always run `pnpm api:generate` before completing a feature** that touches the API to ensure type safety across the monorepo.

3. **Commit the regenerated client files** (`apps/web/src/api/`) along with your API changes.

### File Upload Flow (Reference Implementation)

```typescript
// 1. Generate random file key
const fileKey = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32));
const fileIV = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12)); // GCM uses 96-bit IV

// 2. Encrypt file content
const encryptedFile = await crypto.subtle.encrypt(
  { name: 'AES-GCM', iv: fileIV },
  await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', fileKey, 'AES-GCM', false, ['encrypt']),
  fileContent
);

// 3. Wrap file key with user's public key (ECIES)
const encryptedFileKey = await eciesEncrypt(fileKey, userPublicKey);

// 4. Upload encrypted file to backend → Pinata → get CID
const { cid } = await api.post('/vault/upload', {
  encryptedFile: new Blob([encryptedFile]),
  fileName: file.name, // plaintext OK for server audit
  iv: bytesToHex(fileIV),
});

// 5. Add to folder metadata (all encrypted)
const fileEntry = {
  type: 'file',
  nameEncrypted: await aesEncrypt(file.name, folderKey),
  nameIv: crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12)),
  cid,
  fileKeyEncrypted: encryptedFileKey,
  fileIv: bytesToHex(fileIV),
  size: file.size,
  created: Date.now(),
  modified: Date.now(),
};

// 6. Re-encrypt folder metadata and republish IPNS
await republishFolderIPNS(folderId, updatedMetadata);
```

### IPNS Publishing Pattern

Every write operation (create/rename/move/delete) must:

1. Update the in-memory folder metadata
2. Re-encrypt the entire metadata JSON with the folder key
3. Sign the encrypted metadata with ECDSA private key
4. Call `POST /vault/publish-ipns` with signed entry

**Performance Note:** IPNS publishing is the bottleneck (~2s). Batch operations when possible (e.g., multi-file upload should publish once at the end).

### Session Token Management

```typescript
// Access tokens (15min, memory only)
const accessToken = response.data.accessToken;
// Store in: React context / Zustand / Redux (never localStorage)

// Refresh tokens (7 days, secure storage)
const refreshToken = response.data.refreshToken;
// Store in: HTTP-only cookie (preferred) OR encrypted localStorage

// Token refresh pattern
if (error.response?.status === 401) {
  const newAccessToken = await refreshAccessToken();
  // Retry original request with new token
}
```

## Common Pitfalls & Anti-Patterns

### ❌ Never Do This

1. **Storing keys in plaintext localStorage**

   ```typescript
   // WRONG
   localStorage.setItem('privateKey', privateKeyHex);
   ```

2. **Logging sensitive data**

   ```typescript
   // WRONG
   console.log('User private key:', privateKey);
   console.log('Decrypted file:', fileContent);
   ```

3. **Sending plaintext to server**

   ```typescript
   // WRONG
   await api.post('/vault/upload', { fileContent: file });
   ```

4. **Using sync crypto in main thread**

   ```typescript
   // WRONG (blocks UI for large files)
   const encrypted = aesEncryptSync(largeFile, key);
   ```

### ✅ Correct Patterns

1. **Store keys in memory, clear on logout**

   ```typescript
   // React context for session-scoped state
   const [ecdsaPrivateKey, setEcdsaPrivateKey] = useState<Uint8Array | null>(null);

   const logout = () => {
     setEcdsaPrivateKey(null); // Cleared from memory
     // No disk persistence
   };
   ```

2. **Use Web Workers for large file encryption**

   ```typescript
   const worker = new Worker('./crypto-worker.js');
   worker.postMessage({ fileData, key });
   worker.onmessage = (e) => {
     const encrypted = e.data;
   };
   ```

3. **Always validate IPNS signatures client-side**

   ```typescript
   const messageHash = await sha256(signedEntry.encryptedMetadata);
   const isValid = await ecdsaVerify(messageHash, signedEntry.signature, userPubkey);
   if (!isValid) throw new Error('Metadata tampering detected');
   ```

## MVP Scope Boundaries (v1.0)

### ✅ In Scope

- Multi-method auth (email/pass, OAuth, magic link, external wallet)
- File upload/download (E2E encrypted)
- Folder operations (create/rename/move/delete)
- Web UI (React)
- Desktop mount (macOS FUSE only for v1.0)
- Multi-device sync (IPNS polling, ~30s latency)
- Vault export (data portability)

### ❌ Out of Scope (defer to v1.1+)

- Billing/payments
- File versioning
- Folder sharing
- Search/indexing
- Mobile apps
- Linux/Windows desktop (v1.1)

**When users request out-of-scope features:** Acknowledge the value, but clarify they're post-MVP. Suggest workarounds if applicable.

## Testing Requirements

### Security Test Checklist

- [ ] Private key never logged (search logs for "privateKey", "ecdsa", "0x04")
- [ ] Private key never in localStorage/sessionStorage
- [ ] All file uploads: server receives ciphertext only
- [ ] All folder names: encrypted in IPNS metadata
- [ ] IPNS signature verification passes
- [ ] Wrong private key cannot decrypt vault

### Performance Benchmarks (P95)

- Auth flow: <3s
- File upload (<100MB): <5s
- File download (<100MB): <5s
- IPNS publish: <2s
- Folder create: <1s
- Multi-device sync latency: <30s

## Key Files & Documentation

- [README.md](../README.md) - Project overview, features, tech stack
- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) - Encryption hierarchy, key derivation, threat model
- [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](../docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) - Local setup, running, testing
- [Preliminary/Documentation/IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md](../Preliminary/Documentation/IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md) - 12-week development timeline
- [Preliminary/Documentation/PRD.md](../Preliminary/Documentation/PRD.md) - Product requirements, user journeys, scope
- [Preliminary/Documentation/TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md](../Preliminary/Documentation/TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md) - Encryption, key hierarchy, system design

- [Preliminary/Documentation/DATA_FLOWS.md](../Preliminary/Documentation/DATA_FLOWS.md) - Sequence diagrams, test vectors
- [Preliminary/Documentation/CLIENT_SPECIFICATION.md](../Preliminary/Documentation/CLIENT_SPECIFICATION.md) - Web UI, desktop app specs

**For detailed crypto flows:** See TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md (key hierarchy, encryption primitives) and DATA_FLOWS.md (sequence diagrams, test vectors)

## API Conventions (When Backend Exists)

### Expected Endpoints

- `POST /auth/login` - Authenticate with Web3Auth ID token or SIWE signature
- `GET /auth/nonce` - Get nonce for SIWE flow
- `POST /auth/refresh` - Refresh access token
- `GET /my-vault` - Get encrypted root key + IPNS name
- `POST /my-vault/initialize` - Create vault (first-time setup)
- `POST /vault/upload` - Upload encrypted file → IPFS → return CID
- `POST /vault/publish-ipns` - Publish signed IPNS entry
- `POST /vault/export` - Generate vault export JSON

### Response Patterns

```typescript
// Success
{ success: true, data: { cid: "QmXxxx..." } }

// Error
{ success: false, error: { code: "VAULT_NOT_INITIALIZED", message: "..." } }
```

## Web3Auth Integration Notes

### Group Connections Setup (Dashboard)

Configure in Web3Auth dashboard to link multiple auth methods:

```text
cipherbox-aggregate (group ID)
  ├─ google (Google OAuth)
  ├─ email_passwordless (Magic Link)
  ├─ auth0 (Email/Password via Auth0)
  └─ external_wallets (MetaMask, WalletConnect)
```

### Client Integration

```typescript
import { Web3Auth } from '@web3auth/modal';

const web3auth = new Web3Auth({
  clientId: 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID',
  web3AuthNetwork: 'sapphire_mainnet', // or testnet
  chainConfig: {
    chainNamespace: 'eip155',
    chainId: '0x1', // Ethereum mainnet (or any chain)
  },
});

await web3auth.initModal();
const web3authProvider = await web3auth.connect();

// Get private key (use sparingly, clear from memory ASAP)
const privateKey = await web3authProvider.request({
  method: 'eth_private_key',
});

// Get ID token for CipherBox backend auth
const { idToken } = await web3auth.authenticateUser();
```

## Verification Requirements

### Playwright MCP for Application Testing

**ALWAYS attempt to verify application changes using Playwright MCP** when it is available. This ensures implemented features work correctly at runtime.

**Verification workflow:**

1. Navigate to the app URL (typically `http://localhost:5173`)
2. Wait for page elements to load
3. Capture screenshots for visual verification
4. Verify element existence and content
5. Test interactive features (clicks, form submissions)
6. Verify computed styles match design specifications

**If Playwright MCP is not available:**

- Document what needs manual verification
- Provide step-by-step test instructions
- Flag items that require human review

### Pencil Design Verification

For UI work, verify implementations against Pencil design files:

1. **Design files are at:** `designs/*.pen` (JSON format)
2. **Extract exact values:** Colors (hex), spacing (pixels), typography
3. **Verify CSS matches:** Check both source CSS and computed styles
4. **Document discrepancies:** Include file/line references for fixes

**Key design specs:**

- Colors: `#000000` (background), `#00D084` (primary green)
- Font: JetBrains Mono (400, 600, 700 weights)
- Spacing: 8px, 12px, 16px, 24px, 32px scale

## Questions to Ask When Unclear

1. **Auth-related:** "Does this require Phase 1 (Web3Auth) or Phase 2 (CipherBox backend) authentication?"
2. **Encryption:** "Should this data be encrypted client-side before transmission?"
3. **Keys:** "Which key in the hierarchy (ECDSA private, root folder, subfolder, file) should be used here?"
4. **IPNS:** "Does this operation require republishing an IPNS entry?"
5. **Scope:** "Is this feature in v1.0 MVP scope, or should it be deferred to v1.1+?"

## Final Note

This project prioritizes **cryptographic correctness over convenience**. When in doubt, err on the side of more encryption, more validation, and stricter security. The target user (cypherpunks, crypto enthusiasts) values privacy guarantees more than UX polish.

**For detailed guidance:** Refer to [PRD.md](../Preliminary/Documentation/PRD.md) for product scope, [TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md](../Preliminary/Documentation/TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md) for crypto and system design, and [DATA_FLOWS.md](../Preliminary/Documentation/DATA_FLOWS.md) for test vectors and sequence diagrams.

Privacy-first encrypted cloud storage with decentralized persistence

--- ## What is CipherBox CipherBox is a **technology demonstrator** for privacy-first cloud storage. All encryption happens client-side — the server never sees plaintext data, file names, or encryption keys. Files are stored on IPFS for decentralized persistence, keys are derived deterministically via Web3Auth so the same user always gets the same vault regardless of login method, and data can be exported for independent recovery without CipherBox. ## Acknowledgements This project is inspired by discussions and planning while working on [ChainSafe Files](https://github.com/chainsafe/ui-monorepo). A massive shout-out to all the colleagues I got to work with on the original ChainSafe Files project, who unknowingly contributed to this phoenix rising out of the ashes. ## Features - **Authentication** — Web3Auth MPC Core Kit: email OTP, Google OAuth, magic link, external wallet. MFA via device factor. Same user + any auth method = same vault. - **Encryption** — Client-side AES-256-GCM for files and metadata. ECIES secp256k1 key wrapping (per-file, per-folder random keys). Streaming AES-CTR for large files. - **File Management** — Upload, download, rename, move, delete. Nested folders up to 20 levels. Drag-and-drop. - **Sharing** — User-to-user sharing with ECIES re-wrapping. Link sharing with time-limited access tokens. - **Search** — Client-side encrypted search index across file and folder names. - **Versioning** — File history with point-in-time restore. - **Sync** — Multi-device via IPNS polling (~30s). Conflict detection and resolution. - **Desktop** — macOS, Windows, and Linux via Tauri v2. Virtual filesystem mount (FUSE-T / WinFSP / libfuse). Background sync with system tray. - **Recycle Bin** — 30-day soft-delete with restore. - **TEE Republishing** — Automatic IPNS record refresh every 3 hours via Phala Cloud. Zero-knowledge: keys decrypted only inside hardware enclaves. - **Data Portability** — Full vault export (JSON + encrypted blobs). Standalone recovery with private key — no CipherBox required. ## Architecture Overview ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌───────────────┐ │ Web / Desktop│────▶│ CipherBox │────▶│ PostgreSQL │ │ (Client) │ │ API │ │ (Metadata) │ └──────┬───────┘ └──────┬───────┘ └───────────────┘ │ │ │ Encrypted │ Relay │ blobs │ ▼ ▼ ┌──────────────┐ ┌───────────────┐ │ IPFS │ │ TEE Worker │ │ (Storage) │ │ (IPNS Refresh)│ └──────────────┘ └───────────────┘ ``` The client encrypts everything locally. The API is a zero-knowledge relay — it stores encrypted keys and routes IPFS/IPNS operations but never accesses plaintext. For full cryptographic details, see [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). ## Tech Stack | Component | Technology | | :----------------- | :-------------------------------------------- | | **Frontend** | React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS | | **Backend** | Node.js + NestJS + TypeScript | | **Database** | PostgreSQL 16 | | **Job Queue** | BullMQ + Redis | | **Key Derivation** | Web3Auth MPC Core Kit | | **Storage** | IPFS via Kubo / Pinata | | **Desktop** | Tauri v2 + FUSE-T / WinFSP | | **TEE** | Phala Cloud (IPNS republishing) | | **Crypto** | Web Crypto API (AES-256-GCM, ECIES secp256k1) | ## Project Structure ```text cipher-box/ ├── apps/ │ ├── api/ # NestJS backend │ ├── web/ # React frontend │ └── desktop/ # Tauri v2 desktop app ├── packages/ │ ├── crypto/ # Shared encryption library │ └── api-client/ # Generated typed API client ├── tee-worker/ # Phala Cloud TEE worker ├── tests/ │ ├── e2e/ # Playwright E2E tests │ └── e2e-desktop/ # Desktop E2E tests └── docker/ # Docker Compose (PostgreSQL, IPFS, Redis) ``` ## Getting Started ```bash docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d pnpm install pnpm dev # starts API (:3000) + web (:5173) ``` See [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) for full setup instructions including desktop app, testing, and environment configuration. ## Documentation | Document | Description | | :------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------- | | [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | Encryption hierarchy, key derivation, threat model | | [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) | Local setup, running, testing | | [docs/AUTHENTICATION_ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/AUTHENTICATION_ARCHITECTURE.md) | Auth flow details | | [docs/METADATA_SCHEMAS.md](docs/METADATA_SCHEMAS.md) | All metadata object schemas | | [docs/VAULT_EXPORT_FORMAT.md](docs/VAULT_EXPORT_FORMAT.md) | Export/recovery data format | | [docs/DATABASE_EVOLUTION_PROTOCOL.md](docs/DATABASE_EVOLUTION_PROTOCOL.md) | Migration discipline | | [00-Preliminary-R&D/Documentation/](00-Preliminary-R&D/Documentation/) | Frozen v1 specifications (PRD, API, Data Flows, Client Spec) | ##
